aions_core/agi_existing_models.py: This file integrates local language models already installed on the system (Mistral-7B, Phi-3 modified for Korean, and Bielik-4.5B) into an AI system. It searches for these models on disk, loads them using either transformers library or llama.cpp depending on the model format, and manages switching between them to conserve memory. The system retrieves data chunks from storage and uses keyword matching to find relevant context, then feeds this to the selected model to generate responses. It also includes a Korean syllable compression mechanism and can run multiple models through an ensemble approach for better results.
aions_core/aions_crla_reformed.py: This file creates an integrated system combining a reformed knowledge base with clean seed data, a tournament-based scoring mechanism for selecting between candidate answers, and panic detection for when the knowledge base becomes overloaded. When a user query cannot be answered directly, the system checks if the number of retrieved chunks exceeds a threshold, and if so, generates multiple candidate answers from those chunks and selects the best one using performance metrics. All successful derivations are saved with full tracing information, and facts meeting confidence thresholds are flagged for later validation.
aions_core/aions_style_parameters.py: This file provides a system to control the style of generated responses without changing their factual content, using parameters like formality, brevity, technical language level, friendliness, and confidence. It includes eight preset style profiles (professional, casual, technical, formal, etc.) and applies text transformations like replacing contractions, removing filler words, or adjusting vocabulary to match the desired style. The system can also analyze existing text to detect its current style parameters, and it wraps around a base AIONS response generator to apply styling after facts are determined.
aions_core/evaluator_engine.py: This file scores and evaluates the performance of an AI system across multiple runs, calculating metrics like latency, how often responses come directly from the knowledge base, response quality, and consistency. It processes individual tasks and rounds of execution, generating weighted overall scores (0-100) and letter grades based on different performance dimensions. Results are logged to a CSV scoreboard file, and the system generates human-readable performance reports highlighting strengths and areas needing improvement.
aions_core/server/cbms_outline.py: This file implements a two-step knowledge retrieval strategy: first returning a summary listing of available data without full content, then drilling down to fetch complete content only for selected items. It tracks chunks in two storage tiers (active and parked/quarantined), assigns relevance scores based on keyword overlap and how many other chunks reference each item, and estimates the bandwidth savings from this progressive disclosure approach. The system can be used as a Python module or command-line tool to search, list, and retrieve knowledge chunks with budget constraints.
aions_core/server/conversation_memory.py: This file logs exchanges between a user and system to persistent conversation files, extracts concepts from recent exchanges to create periodic summaries, and detects user profile information like names mentioned during conversation. It provides functions to retrieve relevant conversation history based on a new query, find similar past exchanges, and roll up multiple recent summaries into consolidated session records that can be referenced later.
aions_core/server/korean_keys.py: This file generates short three-character keys from text tokens using both direct character trigrams and hashed derivatives, inspired by Korean syllable structure. These keys are used for efficient text matching and searching, derived from normalizing words and building stable representations that help find semantically similar content even with different phrasing.
aions_core/server/web_rag_cbms.py: This file integrates web crawling with the knowledge base system: when a query cannot be answered locally, it searches trusted websites (Wikipedia, Stack Overflow, GitHub, documentation sites), extracts relevant sentences, scores them by relevance, and temporarily injects them as knowledge chunks so they can be used to answer the original query. It uses safe HTTP fetching with user-agent headers, filters out low-quality sentences, and automatically cleans up temporary injected data after a time window.
aions_core/tools/check_status.py: This file makes a simple HTTP request to a local status endpoint and retrieves error information from a running service.
aions_core/tools/symbolic_probe.py: This file demonstrates converting natural language queries to an intermediate symbolic form (Esperanto), encoding that symbolic form into CBMS codes using a codebook, and searching for matching knowledge chunks based on the symbolic representation. It loads supporting modules dynamically and shows how symbolic matching can find relevant knowledge even when phrasing differs from the original query.
control_plane/__init__.py: This is a marker module for the control plane phase 3 MVP package.
control_plane/blends/__init__.py: This is a marker module for control plane blend learning command-line entry points.
control_plane/llm/__init__.py: This module provides an optional faster HTTP client to a local language model server running Bielik-4.5B as an alternative to the default subprocess-based execution path, with full fallback to the original mechanism if the server is unavailable.
control_plane/node_registry.py: This file manages an in-memory registry of worker nodes with their capabilities, health status, resource usage, and available tools, optionally persisting to JSON. It supports registering new nodes, recording heartbeats to mark nodes as alive, filtering healthy nodes, and selecting the best node for a given task based on required tools and current load.
control_plane/policy.py: This file enforces execution policies by defining which tools are allowed (like system health checks, knowledge base searches, and planning functions) and blocking dangerous intent patterns (like filesystem destructive commands) before they are executed.
This file runs a four-step verification pipeline for new skills being promoted to production: schema validation, Python compilation check, sandboxed execution (with different rigor based on risk level), and logging of results to both local and remote systems. Low-risk skills are actually executed to verify they work, medium/high-risk skills only run dummy commands, and all results are appended to a verification log.
control_plane/skills/recipes.py: This file stores successful execution plans (recipes) that solved particular problems, along with why they worked, so similar future requests can reuse them. It integrates with a semantic search system to find recipes when a paraphrased version of a past problem is requested, maintaining a threshold above false-positives while catching true paraphrases.
This file is a wrapper that changes the current working directory before launching an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, fixing a Windows-specific issue where the IDE ignores the working directory configuration.
mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/llm_mou: This file provides a thin language model interface (Qwen) that parses user intent and rephrases facts into conversational replies. It supports multiple backends (Ollama, in-process GGUF, and HTTP GGUF server) with fallback behavior, has system prompts that enforce the model never invents facts or pretends to call tools, and can match user language preferences when generating responses.
scripts/aions_indexer.py: This file builds or inspects a searchable index of the Linux filesystem by scanning a configured set of directories and storing metadata in JSON format, with auto-refresh capability to detect changes.
scripts/chatgpt_extractor.py: This file extracts ChatGPT conversation history and custom GPT definitions from the desktop application's cache directories (LevelDB and IndexedDB), parsing binary files to recover conversation IDs, titles, and message content, then saves the extracted data as JSON summaries and readable text files.
scripts/demo_train.py: This file demonstrates a skill training workflow: learning recipes by composing steps and verifying they work, repeating successful patterns to build confidence, and testing newly available skills against various commands to monitor which ones are most useful.
scripts/ingest_tier1_chroma.py: This file loads critical knowledge base metadata and operator profile information into a semantic search database (Chroma), enforcing version compatibility with the existing database format and selecting a prioritized sample of knowledge chunks for fast access.
scripts/register_treasure_chunk.py: This file registers a single metadata chunk describing the location and status of stored artifacts (backups, indexes, data archives) so they can be discovered and referenced through the knowledge base system.
scripts/test_forge.py: This file end-to-end tests the skill creation and deployment pipeline: requesting a new skill, simulating its construction with metadata and handler code, promoting it through verification, confirming it works when executed, detecting that a related capability gap still exists, and cleaning up test artifacts.
scripts/turbo_scanner.py: This file rapidly indexes an entire codebase using the Windows Everything tool for instant file location, then processes files in parallel to extract metadata (size, line count, imports), detects duplicates by hash, builds a dependency graph, and identifies hub files (frequently imported) and orphan files (never referenced).
scripts/verify_tier1_chroma.py: This file checks that the semantic search database (Chroma) was loaded correctly by searching for expected operator profile and knowledge base records and verifying that minimum document counts and search results are present.
server/store_api.py: This file provides an HTTP client that mirrors the interface of an embedded knowledge base by routing requests to a remote API server, including methods to add items, search, list sessions, and retrieve statistics about stored data.
